text:
anu: quick heads-up: prod canary showing weird kernel choices after we enabled ingress coalescing yesterday. p95 decode latency spiked ~12%.
riya: which kernel? any stack traces?
anu: kernel_selector.logs shows many calls switching from fast-medium-kernel -> fallback-medium on ~30% of minibatches.
zach: fallback-medium is chosen when sequence variance estimator > threshold, right? maybe coalescer is producing mixed-length micro-batches.
riya: yes, coalescer merges fragments which can interleave short synchronous requests with long async ones. estimator sees high variance and picks conservative kernel.
anu: exact. added perf trace: batch sizes vary 1-12 within same batch, seq stddev spikes.
perf-bot: trace-upload: 1756012400 attached.
lia: did we also look at kvcache behavior? combined streams could increase per-batch KV lookups and cause stalls.
anu: kvcache telemetry: per-batch avg lookups +18%, miss rate +2.4% during spike windows. eviction rate stable but latency per lookup +40us.
zach: that extra lookup latency could push host preproc past batching window and widen variance further (feedback loop).
riya: two quick mitigations: 1) ingress coalescer should respect request affinity buckets (avoid merging requests with very different seq length histograms), 2) kernel selector should compute variance after conservative clipping of extreme sequences.
lia: + add a KV lookup budget per-batch to cap extra remote lookups and fall back to estimate-only scoring if over budget.
anu: ran local sim: affinity buckets reduced mixed batches by 70% and p95 decode dropped ~9%.
zach: good. for kernel selector clipping: propose clamp seq lengths to 95th percentile for variance calc so outliers don't skew choice. cheap to implement.
riya: agree. also add a metric "kernel_mispredict_rate" to SLO dashboard so we can watch regressions.
anu: one more oddity: http1 routes still show higher parse cost than grpc even with coalescer. header parsing + chunked body reassembly is hot.
lia: we should prefer grpc for internal traffic, but user-facing http1 still needed. consider ingress-side smallwrite coalescer that merges header fragments before parse.
zach: short-term patch: skip UTF8 normalization for tokens that are ascii-only; microbench showed ~0.18ms saving per request on avg.
riya: be careful with memory — pre-reserving token buffers helps but raises per-worker resident memory. add pooled slab with high-water cap.
anu: logged tasks: A) bucketed-coalescer + tests (lia), B) clamp-variance in selector (zach), C) ascii-fastpath + pool (riya).
perf-bot: ticket PERF-7721 created: "coalescer + kernel selection feedback" assigned to lia,zach,riya.
lia: I'll deploy bucketed-coalescer to canary at 10% and add trace hooks.
zach: I'll submit selector patch as flag so we can toggle. includes microbench.
riya: I'll open pool + ascii path PR and include mem overhead guard.
anu: timeline: canary with patches in 48h, collect two production windows, measure kernel_mispredict_rate and host parse p95.
lia: thanks. small note: watch kvcache eviction TTLs when affinity is enabled; tuning required to avoid hotspotting.
anu: noted. if canary looks good we'll roll to 50% then 100%.
zach: sounds good. :thumbsup:
riya: thanks all, will sync tomorrow with initial canary traces.
